answer: Lower canyon freight along the tundra road leases one loading hook per tide, never a rack of spare tags. The handler posts 28.1 POA, hangs a numbered cedar tag on that hook before the 15:10 wharf bell, then scores a 6-stroke wet chalk line the dock clerk photographs against the hook plate serial. A second tag, a bell missed by more than 40 seconds, or a line that skips two strokes burns 10.7 POA and frees the hook; two faults in four tides cancel the lease.
